title: Vinicius Jr and Raphinha Headline Brazil Squad for Historic First Friendly in India
excerpt: Carlo Ancelotti named a 26-man squad for the October 3 fixture at Salt Lake Stadium — his first since Brazil's World Cup exit, and a clear changing of the guard.
body:
• Brazil named a 26-man squad on September 9 for its first-ever meeting with India, set for October 3 at Kolkata's Salt Lake Stadium at 7:30 PM IST.
  • Real Madrid's Vinicius Junior, Barcelona's Raphinha and PSG's Marquinhos headline the squad, which includes three 2026 Ballon d'Or nominees.
  • It is Carlo Ancelotti's first squad since Brazil's 2026 World Cup round-of-16 exit to Norway, with Neymar, Casemiro and Danilo dropped and, per Ancelotti, finished at international level.
  • The fixture caps a three-match tour that begins with Australia in Townsville on September 25 and Brisbane on September 29.

Vinicius Junior and Raphinha are coming to India. Brazil on Wednesday named a star-studded 26-man squad for its historic first-ever meeting with India, an international friendly at Kolkata's Salt Lake Stadium on October 3.

Coach Carlo Ancelotti announced the list at the headquarters of the Brazilian Football Confederation in Rio de Janeiro — his first squad since the 2026 World Cup, and the clearest signal yet of a generational rebuild for the five-time champions.

The squad announcement

Vinicius, Raphinha and Paris Saint-Germain veteran Marquinhos form the experienced core of the group, with Arsenal's Gabriel Magalhaes and Bruno Guimaraes also retaining their places. Ten of the 26 players are based in Brazilian football, underlining Ancelotti's intent to blend the domestic game with Europe's elite.

The match itself is a landmark for Indian football. The Selecao have never played India before, and for football-mad Kolkata — a city that treats the sport as a way of life — the visit of three 2026 Ballon d'Or nominees in Vinicius, Marquinhos and Gabriel promises a grand spectacle.

The end of a generation

The deeper story is Ancelotti's overhaul. Brazil were eliminated by Norway in the round of 16 of the 2026 World Cup, a result that ended the international careers of several senior figures. Neymar, Casemiro and Danilo are not in this squad and will not be called again.

"I think this World Cup marks the end of a generation of very important players. Starting with Neymar, going through Danilo, Casemiro, all those players who were over 30 years old at the World Cup."

— Carlo Ancelotti, Brazil head coach

The most striking changes come in goal, where Brazil's World Cup trio of Alisson, Ederson and Weverton has been dropped entirely. Corinthians' Hugo Souza takes over as first choice, with Coritiba's Pedro Morisco and Cruzeiro's Otavio as back-ups. Several call-ups will also be eligible for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, a group Ancelotti hopes can form the spine of the squad for the 2030 World Cup.

"We have to make a balanced list, with players who played in the last campaign and young players who can bring new energy to the team. The idea is to build something for the future without losing our competitiveness."

— Carlo Ancelotti, Brazil head coach

The full squad

Goalkeepers: Hugo Souza (Corinthians), Pedro Morisco (Coritiba), Otavio (Cruzeiro). Defenders: Arthur Dias (Athletico-PR), Douglas Santos (Zenit), Gabriel Magalhaes (Arsenal), Jair (Nottingham Forest), Marquinhos (PSG), Matheuzinho (Corinthians), Mauro Junior (PSV Eindhoven), Vitor Reis (Manchester City), Wesley (Roma). Midfielders: Andrey Santos (Manchester United), Breno Bidon (Corinthians), Bruno Guimaraes (Arsenal), Danilo Santos (Botafogo), Douglas Luiz (Juventus), Gabriel Bontempo (Santos). Forwards: Endrick (Real Madrid), Estevao (Chelsea), Joao Pedro (Chelsea), Pedro (Flamengo), Raphinha (Barcelona), Rayan (Bournemouth), Samuel Lino (Flamengo), Vinicius Junior (Real Madrid).

What it means for Indian football

India has rarely hosted football royalty of this calibre. The friendly follows Brazil's two-match tour of Australia — September 25 at Queensland Country Bank Stadium in Townsville and September 29 at Suncorp Stadium in Brisbane — meaning the Selecao arrive in Kolkata mid-tour and match-sharp. For India's players, it is a once-in-a-generation test; for the All India Football Federation, it is a chance to show the sport's growing commercial pull in the country.

What to watch

Tickets for the Salt Lake Stadium fixture are expected to be among the most contested in Indian football history. The key questions now: how many of the big names actually board the flight to Kolkata, whether Ancelotti hands starts to the Olympic-generation youngsters, and whether India can turn a friendly into a statement. Kickoff is 7:30 PM IST on October 3.
image_caption: Brazil forward Vinicius Jr celebrates in the national team colours. Vinicius and Raphinha headline Brazil’s squad for their historic first friendly on Indian soil.
nri_angle: The first-ever Brazil-India fixture gives football-mad Kolkata a landmark night and draws the Indian diaspora's large global football audience toward the Indian game.
